50	/** Radius of the shell the division clusters sit on. */
51	const SHELL_RADIUS = 66
52	
53	/** How far the shell is flattened vertically, so the graph reads as a body. */
54	const SHELL_FLATTEN = 0.56
55	
56	/** Relaxation passes; enough for a stable picture, cheap enough to run on mount. */
57	const PASSES = 260
58	
59	/**
60	 * Deterministic 32-bit PRNG, so the same roster always lays out identically.
61	 * @param seed - Any 32-bit integer.
62	 * @returns A function returning the next float in `[0, 1)`.
63	 */
64	function rng(seed: number): () => number {
65	  let state = seed >>> 0
66	  return () => {
67	    state = (state + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0
68	    let t = state
69	    t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1)
70	    t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61)
71	    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296
72	  }
73	}
74	
75	/**
76	 * Lay out one roster.
77	 * @param roster - The roster to place.
78	 * @returns Node positions, cluster anchors, and the index the scene reads.
79	 */
80	export function layoutRoster(roster: Roster): GraphLayout {
81	  const next = rng(0xc0ffee)
82	  const divisions = roster.divisions.map(entry => entry.id)
83	  const centres = new Map<string, { x: number; y: number; z: number }>()
84	
85	  // Clusters sit on a flattened Fibonacci shell: evenly spread in every
86	  // direction, so no orbit angle stacks two divisions on top of each other,
87	  // while the flattening keeps the whole graph inside a readable frame.
88	  const golden = Math.PI * (3 - Math.sqrt(5))
89	  for (const [ordinal, id] of divisions.entries()) {
90	    const height = 1 - ((ordinal / Math.max(1, divisions.length - 1)) * 2)
91	    const ring = Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, 1 - (height * height)))
92	    const angle = golden * ordinal
93	    centres.set(id, {
94	      x: Math.cos(angle) * ring * SHELL_RADIUS,
95	      y: height * SHELL_RADIUS * SHELL_FLATTEN,
96	      z: Math.sin(angle) * ring * SHELL_RADIUS,
97	    })
98	  }
99	
100	  const nodes: GraphNode[] = roster.agents.map((agent) => {
101	    const centre = centres.get(agent.division) ?? { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 }
102	    return {
103	      id: agent.id,
104	      division: agent.division,
105	      x: centre.x + (next() - 0.5) * 22,
106	      y: centre.y + (next() - 0.5) * 22,
107	      z: centre.z + (next() - 0.5) * 22,
108	    }
109	  })
110	
111	  const index = new Map<string, number>()
112	  for (const [ordinal, node] of nodes.entries()) index.set(node.id, ordinal)
113	
114	  const springs = roster.edges
115	    .map(edge => ({ a: index.get(edge.from), b: index.get(edge.to) }))
116	    .filter((pair): pair is { a: number; b: number } => pair.a !== undefined && pair.b !== undefined)
117	
118	  // Repulsion runs inside a division only: 147 nodes squared every pass is
119	  // affordable, but keeping it local is what preserves the cluster reading.
120	  const byDivision = new Map<string, number[]>()
121	  for (const [ordinal, node] of nodes.entries()) {
122	    const list = byDivision.get(node.division) ?? []
123	    list.push(ordinal)
124	    byDivision.set(node.division, list)
125	  }
126	
127	  for (let pass = 0; pass < PASSES; pass++) {
128	    const cooling = 1 - (pass / PASSES)
129	
130	    for (const group of byDivision.values()) {
131	      for (let i = 0; i < group.length; i++) {
132	        for (let j = i + 1; j < group.length; j++) {
133	          const firstIndex = group[i]
134	          const secondIndex = group[j]
135	          if (firstIndex === undefined || secondIndex === undefined) continue
136	          const first = nodes[firstIndex]
137	          const second = nodes[secondIndex]
138	          if (first === undefined || second === undefined) continue
139	          const dx = second.x - first.x
140	          const dy = second.y - first.y
141	          const dz = second.z - first.z
142	          const distanceSquared = (dx * dx) + (dy * dy) + (dz * dz) + 0.01

144	          const distance = Math.sqrt(distanceSquared)
145	          const ux = (dx / distance) * push
146	          const uy = (dy / distance) * push
147	          const uz = (dz / distance) * push

149	          first.y -= uy
150	          first.z -= uz
151	          second.x += ux
152	          second.y += uy
153	          second.z += uz

155	      }
156	    }
157	
158	    for (const spring of springs) {
159	      const first = nodes[spring.a]
160	      const second = nodes[spring.b]
161	      if (first === undefined || second === undefined) continue

163	      const dy = second.y - first.y
164	      const dz = second.z - first.z

168	      first.y += dy * pull

204	    const count = Math.max(members.length, 1)

40	 * @param layout - The computed layout, whose extent frames the whole roster.
41	 * @returns The resting shot.
42	 */
43	function restingShot(layout: GraphLayout): Shot {
44	  return {
45	    position: new Vector3(0, layout.extent * 0.26, layout.extent * 2.2),
46	    target: new Vector3(0, 0, 0),
47	  }
48	}

50	/**
51	 * The shot the deck opens on: far enough out that the graph reads as one body
52	 * in the haze, and high enough that the flight down has somewhere to go.
53	 * @param layout - The computed layout, whose extent sets the distance.
54	 * @returns The establishing shot.
55	 */
56	function establishingShot(layout: GraphLayout): Shot {
57	  return {
58	    position: new Vector3(layout.extent * 0.85, layout.extent * 1.35, layout.extent * 3),
59	    target: new Vector3(0, 0, 0),
60	  }
61	}

63	/**
64	 * The shot that frames one agent.
65	 *
66	 * The approach keeps the direction the camera is already looking from: the
67	 * agent was clicked because it was visible, so nothing stands between that
68	 * direction and it, and the flight reads as closing in on what was picked
69	 * rather than as a cut to somewhere else.
70	 * @param x - The agent's world x.
71	 * @param y - The agent's world y.
72	 * @param z - The agent's world z.
73	 * @param from - Where the camera is now.
74	 * @returns A shot looking at the agent from just outside it.
75	 */
76	function focusShot(x: number, y: number, z: number, from: Vector3): Shot {
77	  const target = new Vector3(x, y, z)
78	  const approach = from.clone().sub(target)
79	  if (approach.lengthSq() < 1) approach.copy(target).normalize()
80	  approach.normalize().multiplyScalar(FOCUS_DISTANCE)
81	  return { position: target.clone().add(approach).add(new Vector3(0, FOCUS_LIFT, 0)), target }
82	}

84	/**
85	 * Camera behaviour: the opening flight, a slow orbit at rest, and a flight to
86	 * and back from the selected agent.
87	 *
88	 * Every move is a timed cubic ease rather than a per-frame approach, so the
89	 * opening shot lands on the beat it was written for instead of drifting with
90	 * the frame rate. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the deck opens at rest and
91	 * selection cuts straight to its shot.
92	 * @param props - The computed layout, which supplies every shot.
93	 * @returns The controls.
94	 */
95	export function CameraRig({ layout }: { layout: GraphLayout }): ReactNode {
96	  const controls = useRef<ElementRef<typeof OrbitControls>>(null)
97	  const reduced = usePrefersReducedMotion()
98	  const selectedId = useDeck(state => state.selectedAgentId)
99	  const { camera } = useThree()
100	  const flight = useRef<Flight | undefined>(undefined)
101	  const opened = useRef(false)
102	  const [resting, setResting] = useState(false)
103	
104	  // The hook's first value is `false` so a server render and the first client
105	  // render agree; the opening shot is decided before that resolves, so it asks
106	  // the media query itself.
107	  const [reducedAtMount] = useState(
108	    () => typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches,
109	  )
110	
111	  const resting3D = useMemo(() => restingShot(layout), [layout])
112	
113	  useLayoutEffect(() => {
114	    if (reducedAtMount) return
115	    const opening = establishingShot(layout)
116	    camera.position.copy(opening.position)
117	  }, [camera, layout, reducedAtMount])
118	
119	  useEffect(() => {
120	    const control = controls.current
121	    if (control === null) return
122	    const node = selectedId === undefined ? undefined : layout.nodes[layout.index.get(selectedId) ?? -1]
123	    if (selectedId !== undefined && node === undefined) return
124	    const to = node === undefined ? resting3D : focusShot(node.x, node.y, node.z, camera.position)
125	    const first = !opened.current
126	    opened.current = true
127	
128	    if (reduced) {
129	      flight.current = undefined
130	      camera.position.copy(to.position)
131	      control.target.copy(to.target)
132	      setResting(true)
133	      return
134	    }
135	
136	    flight.current = {
137	      from: { position: camera.position.clone(), target: control.target.clone() },
138	      to,
139	      started: performance.now(),
140	      duration: first ? ESTABLISH_MS : FOCUS_MS,
141	    }
142	    setResting(false)
143	  }, [camera, layout, reduced, resting3D, selectedId])
144	
145	  useFrame(() => {
146	    const control = controls.current
147	    if (control === null) return
148	    const move = flight.current
149	    if (move !== undefined) {
150	      const progress = Math.min(1, (performance.now() - move.started) / move.duration)
151	      const eased = easeInOutCubic(progress)
152	      camera.position.lerpVectors(move.from.position, move.to.position, eased)
153	      control.target.lerpVectors(move.from.target, move.to.target, eased)
154	      if (progress >= 1) {
155	        flight.current = undefined
156	        setResting(true)
157	      }
158	    }
159	    control.update()
160	  })
161	
162	  return (
163	    <OrbitControls
164	      ref={controls}
165	      makeDefault
166	      enableDamping
167	      dampingFactor={0.06}
168	      rotateSpeed={0.5}
169	      zoomSpeed={0.7}
170	      minDistance={18}
171	      maxDistance={420}
172	      // A drag takes the camera over: the opening flight is a shot, not a lock,
173	      // and the orbit it was flying into resumes from wherever the drag ends.
174	      onStart={() => {
175	        flight.current = undefined
176	        setResting(true)
177	      }}
178	      autoRotate={!reduced && resting && selectedId === undefined}
179	      autoRotateSpeed={0.28}
180	    />
181	  )
182	}

11	import { BufferAttribute, BufferGeometry, Color, Vector3 } from 'three'
12	import type { RosterEdge } from '@/deck/contract'
13	import type { GraphLayout } from '@/deck/layout-enterprise'
14	import { EDGE_COLOR } from '@/deck/palette'
15	
16	/** Segments each curved edge is drawn with. */
17	const EDGE_SEGMENTS = 10
18	
19	/** How far an edge bows towards the graph centre, as a share of its length. */
20	const EDGE_SAG = 0.22
21	
22	/** One relationship as the arc both the line layer and the traffic layer ride. */
23	export interface EdgeArc {
24	  /** The source agent's node position; traffic starts here. */
25	  from: Vector3
26	  /** The Bézier control point, pulled towards the graph centre. */
27	  mid: Vector3
28	  /** The target agent's node position; traffic ends here. */
29	  to: Vector3
30	  colour: Color
31	  fromId: string
32	  toId: string
33	}
34	
35	const SCRATCH_MID = new Vector3()
36	
37	/**
38	 * Resolve the roster's relationships onto the laid-out graph.
39	 * @param edges - The relationships to place.
40	 * @param layout - The computed layout supplying node positions.
41	 * @returns One arc per edge whose endpoints both exist in the layout.
42	 */
43	export function buildArcs(edges: readonly RosterEdge[], layout: GraphLayout): EdgeArc[] {
44	  const arcs: EdgeArc[] = []
45	  for (const edge of edges) {
46	    const a = layout.nodes[layout.index.get(edge.from) ?? -1]
47	    const b = layout.nodes[layout.index.get(edge.to) ?? -1]
48	    if (a === undefined || b === undefined) continue
49	    const from = new Vector3(a.x, a.y, a.z)
50	    const to = new Vector3(b.x, b.y, b.z)
51	    const mid = SCRATCH_MID.copy(from).add(to).multiplyScalar(0.5 * (1 - EDGE_SAG)).clone()
52	    arcs.push({ from, mid, to, colour: new Color(EDGE_COLOR[edge.kind]), fromId: edge.from, toId: edge.to })
53	  }
54	  return arcs
55	}
56	
57	/**
58	 * Evaluate one arc.
59	 * @param arc - The arc to sample.
60	 * @param t - Position along the arc, `0` at the source and `1` at the target.
61	 * @param out - Vector the result is written into.
62	 * @returns `out`, for chaining.
63	 */
64	export function arcPoint(arc: EdgeArc, t: number, out: Vector3): Vector3 {
65	  const inverse = 1 - t
66	  return out.set(0, 0, 0)
67	    .addScaledVector(arc.from, inverse * inverse)
68	    .addScaledVector(arc.mid, 2 * inverse * t)
69	    .addScaledVector(arc.to, t * t)
70	}
71	
72	/**
73	 * Build one line-segment geometry for a set of arcs.
74	 *
75	 * Each arc dims towards its middle, so the endpoints — the agents — stay the
76	 * brightest thing in the layer.
77	 * @param arcs - The arcs to draw.
78	 * @returns A geometry with `position` and `color` attributes.
79	 */
80	export function buildEdgeGeometry(arcs: readonly EdgeArc[]): BufferGeometry {
81	  const vertices = arcs.length * EDGE_SEGMENTS * 2
82	  const positions = new Float32Array(vertices * 3)
83	  const colors = new Float32Array(vertices * 3)
84	  const point = new Vector3()
85	  let cursor = 0
86	
87	  for (const arc of arcs) {
88	    for (let segment = 0; segment < EDGE_SEGMENTS; segment++) {
89	      for (const end of [segment / EDGE_SEGMENTS, (segment + 1) / EDGE_SEGMENTS]) {
90	        arcPoint(arc, end, point)
91	        const fade = 0.25 + (Math.abs(end - 0.5) * 1.5)
92	        positions[cursor * 3] = point.x
93	        positions[(cursor * 3) + 1] = point.y
94	        positions[(cursor * 3) + 2] = point.z
95	        colors[cursor * 3] = arc.colour.r * fade
96	        colors[(cursor * 3) + 1] = arc.colour.g * fade
97	        colors[(cursor * 3) + 2] = arc.colour.b * fade
98	        cursor += 1
99	      }
100	    }
101	  }
102	
103	  const built = new BufferGeometry()
104	  built.setAttribute('position', new BufferAttribute(positions, 3))
105	  built.setAttribute('color', new BufferAttribute(colors, 3))
106	  return built
107	}

// Drive the pre-installed Chromium over CDP: navigate, settle, screenshot.
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { setTimeout as sleep } from 'node:timers/promises'

const [, , outDir, widthArg, heightArg, ...targets] = process.argv
const width = Number(widthArg)
const height = Number(heightArg)
mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true })

const PORT = 9333
const chrome = spawn('/opt/pw-browsers/chromium', [
  '--headless=new',
  '--no-sandbox',
  '--disable-dev-shm-usage',
  '--enable-unsafe-swiftshader',
  '--hide-scrollbars',
  '--force-device-scale-factor=1',
  `--window-size=${width},${height}`,
  `--remote-debugging-port=${PORT}`,
  'about:blank',
], { stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] })

chrome.stderr.on('data', () => {})

async function targetsList() {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 60; attempt++) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`)
      const list = await res.json()
      const page = list.find(t => t.type === 'page')
      if (page) return page
    } catch {}
    await sleep(400)
  }
  throw new Error('chromium devtools never came up')
}

const page = await targetsList()
const ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl)
await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
  ws.addEventListener('open', resolve, { once: true })
  ws.addEventListener('error', reject, { once: true })
})

let nextId = 0
const pending = new Map()
const events = new Map()
ws.addEventListener('message', (message) => {
  const payload = JSON.parse(message.data)
  if (payload.id !== undefined) {
    const entry = pending.get(payload.id)
    pending.delete(payload.id)
    if (entry) entry.resolve(payload.result ?? payload.error)
    return
  }
  const waiters = events.get(payload.method) ?? []
  events.set(payload.method, [])
  for (const waiter of waiters) waiter(payload.params)
})

function send(method, params = {}) {
  const id = ++nextId
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    pending.set(id, { resolve })
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }))
  })
}

function once(method, timeoutMs = 20000) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const list = events.get(method) ?? []
    list.push(resolve)
    events.set(method, list)
    setTimeout(() => resolve(undefined), timeoutMs)
  })
}

await send('Page.enable')
await send('Runtime.enable')
await send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride', {
  width, height, deviceScaleFactor: 1, mobile: width < 700,
})

for (const target of targets) {
  const [name, url, settleArg, script] = target.split('::')
  const settle = Number(settleArg ?? 6000)
  const loaded = once('Page.loadEventFired')
  await send('Page.navigate', { url })
  await loaded
  await sleep(settle)
  if (script) {
    const result = await send('Runtime.evaluate', { expression: script, awaitPromise: true })
    if (result?.exceptionDetails) console.error(name, 'script error', JSON.stringify(result.exceptionDetails).slice(0, 300))
    await sleep(2200)
  }
  const shot = await send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png', captureBeyondViewport: false })
  if (!shot?.data) {
    console.error(`${name}: no screenshot data`, JSON.stringify(shot).slice(0, 200))
    continue
  }
  writeFileSync(`${outDir}/${name}.png`, Buffer.from(shot.data, 'base64'))
  console.log(`${name}.png`)
}

ws.close()
chrome.kill('SIGKILL')
process.exit(0)

1	'use client'
2	
3	import { useFrame, useThree } from '@react-three/fiber'
4	import { useEffect, useLayoutEffect, useMemo, useRef, type ReactNode } from 'react'
5	import {
6	  AdditiveBlending,
7	  Color,
8	  DoubleSide,
9	  Euler,
10	  Matrix4,
11	  Quaternion,
12	  Vector3,
13	  type InstancedMesh,
14	} from 'three'
15	import type { GraphLayout } from '@/deck/layout-enterprise'
16	import { usePrefersReducedMotion } from '@/deck/motion'
17	import { useDeck } from '@/deck/store'
18	import { createBeamGeometry } from './sprites.ts'
19	
20	/** How many certificate bursts can be on screen at once. */
21	const BURST_POOL = 8
22	
23	/** Lifetime of one certificate burst, in milliseconds. */
24	const BURST_MS = 1_600
25	
26	/** The colour a certificate is issued in, matching the deck's `--green`. */
27	const BURST_COLOR = '#49e0a6'
28	
29	/** Radius the ring starts and ends at, in world units. */
30	const RING = { from: 1.4, to: 9.5 }
31	
32	/** Width and height of the light beam at full rise, in world units. */
33	const BEAM = { width: 2.2, height: 19 }
34	
35	/** Peak brightness of the ring and of the beam, before the burst fades. */
36	const RING_GAIN = 0.62
37	const BEAM_GAIN = 0.4
38	
39	const SCRATCH_MATRIX = new Matrix4()
40	const SCRATCH_SCALE = new Vector3()
41	const SCRATCH_POSITION = new Vector3()
42	const SCRATCH_QUATERNION = new Quaternion()
43	const SCRATCH_EULER = new Euler()
44	const SCRATCH_COLOR = new Color()
45	const BASE_COLOR = new Color(BURST_COLOR)
46	const ZERO_SCALE = new Vector3(0, 0, 0)
47	
48	/**
49	 * Where a certificate was just issued: an expanding ring around the agent and
50	 * a short beam of light standing on it.
51	 *
52	 * Both are instanced over one pool, so a run that certifies six agents at once
53	 * still costs two draw calls. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the ring and the
54	 * beam hold their size and then cut, instead of expanding and fading.
55	 * @param props - The computed layout, used to place each burst on its agent.
56	 * @returns The burst layers.
57	 */
58	export function CertificateBursts({ layout }: { layout: GraphLayout }): ReactNode {
59	  const reduced = usePrefersReducedMotion()
60	  const bursts = useDeck(state => state.bursts)
61	  const rings = useRef<InstancedMesh>(null)
62	  const beams = useRef<InstancedMesh>(null)
63	  const { camera } = useThree()
64	
65	  const beamGeometry = useMemo(createBeamGeometry, [])
66	  useEffect(() => () => beamGeometry.dispose(), [beamGeometry])
67	
68	  const pool = useMemo(() => ({
69	    position: new Float32Array(BURST_POOL * 3),
70	    started: new Float64Array(BURST_POOL),
71	    cursor: 0,
72	  }), [])
73	
74	  // Seeding both instance colour buffers before the first frame is what keeps
75	  // the first certificate of a run from compiling a shader as it lands.
76	  useLayoutEffect(() => {
77	    const ring = rings.current
78	    const beam = beams.current
79	    if (ring === null || beam === null) return
80	    SCRATCH_COLOR.setScalar(0)
81	    for (let slot = 0; slot < BURST_POOL; slot++) {
82	      ring.setColorAt(slot, SCRATCH_COLOR)
83	      beam.setColorAt(slot, SCRATCH_COLOR)
84	    }
85	    if (ring.instanceColor !== null) ring.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true
86	    if (beam.instanceColor !== null) beam.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true
87	  }, [])
88	
89	  useFrame(() => {
90	    const ring = rings.current
91	    const beam = beams.current
92	    if (ring === null || beam === null) return
93	    const now = performance.now()
94	
95	    // Drain the store's queue: every burst is drawn once, then forgotten.
96	    while (bursts.length > 0) {
97	      const burst = bursts.shift()
98	      if (burst === undefined) break
99	      const node = layout.nodes[layout.index.get(burst.agentId) ?? -1]
100	      if (node === undefined) continue
101	      const slot = pool.cursor
102	      pool.position[slot * 3] = node.x
103	      pool.position[(slot * 3) + 1] = node.y
104	      pool.position[(slot * 3) + 2] = node.z
105	      pool.started[slot] = now
106	      pool.cursor = (pool.cursor + 1) % BURST_POOL
107	    }
108	
109	    for (let slot = 0; slot < BURST_POOL; slot++) {
110	      const started = pool.started[slot] ?? 0
111	      const age = started === 0 ? 1 : (now - started) / BURST_MS
112	      if (age >= 1) {
113	        SCRATCH_MATRIX.compose(SCRATCH_POSITION.set(0, 0, 0), SCRATCH_QUATERNION.identity(), ZERO_SCALE)
114	        ring.setMatrixAt(slot, SCRATCH_MATRIX)
115	        beam.setMatrixAt(slot, SCRATCH_MATRIX)
116	        continue
117	      }
118	
119	      SCRATCH_POSITION.set(
120	        pool.position[slot * 3] ?? 0,
121	        pool.position[(slot * 3) + 1] ?? 0,
122	        pool.position[(slot * 3) + 2] ?? 0,
123	      )
124	      const spread = reduced ? 0.55 : 1 - ((1 - age) ** 2)
125	      const fade = reduced ? 1 : (1 - age) ** 1.4
126	
127	      SCRATCH_SCALE.setScalar(RING.from + (spread * (RING.to - RING.from)))
128	      SCRATCH_MATRIX.compose(SCRATCH_POSITION, camera.quaternion, SCRATCH_SCALE)
129	      ring.setMatrixAt(slot, SCRATCH_MATRIX)
130	      ring.setColorAt(slot, SCRATCH_COLOR.copy(BASE_COLOR).multiplyScalar(fade * RING_GAIN))
131	
132	      // The beam stands upright and turns on its own axis to face the camera,
133	      // so it reads as a shaft of light rather than a card.
134	      const yaw = Math.atan2(camera.position.x - SCRATCH_POSITION.x, camera.position.z - SCRATCH_POSITION.z)
135	      SCRATCH_QUATERNION.setFromEuler(SCRATCH_EULER.set(0, yaw, 0))
136	      SCRATCH_SCALE.set(BEAM.width, BEAM.height * (reduced ? 1 : Math.min(1, age * 3.2)), 1)
137	      SCRATCH_MATRIX.compose(SCRATCH_POSITION, SCRATCH_QUATERNION, SCRATCH_SCALE)
138	      beam.setMatrixAt(slot, SCRATCH_MATRIX)
139	      beam.setColorAt(slot, SCRATCH_COLOR.copy(BASE_COLOR).multiplyScalar(fade * BEAM_GAIN))
140	    }
141	
142	    ring.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true
143	    beam.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true
144	    if (ring.instanceColor !== null) ring.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true
145	    if (beam.instanceColor !== null) beam.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true
146	  })
147	
148	  return (
149	    <group>
150	      <instancedMesh ref={rings} args={[undefined, undefined, BURST_POOL]} frustumCulled={false}>
151	        <ringGeometry args={[0.84, 1, 48]} />
152	        <meshBasicMaterial
153	          transparent
154	          side={DoubleSide}
155	          blending={AdditiveBlending}
156	          depthWrite={false}
157	          toneMapped={false}
158	        />
159	      </instancedMesh>
160	
161	      <instancedMesh ref={beams} args={[beamGeometry, undefined, BURST_POOL]} frustumCulled={false}>
162	        <meshBasicMaterial
163	          vertexColors
164	          transparent
165	          side={DoubleSide}
166	          blending={AdditiveBlending}
167	          depthWrite={false}
168	          toneMapped={false}
169	        />
170	      </instancedMesh>
171	    </group>
172	  )
173	}

type PresentationMode = 'off' | 'focus' | 'tour'

/**
 * How far the cold open has got.
 *
 * It runs at most once per page load: `idle` is a deck that has not opened,
 * `playing` the sequence itself, and `done` a deck that has already assembled,
 * which is why a second tour starts on its first view instead of replaying it.
 */
export type OpeningPhase = 'idle' | 'playing' | 'done'

/**
 * Frame state the cold open drives.
 *
 * `reveal` walks from 0, with the graph dark, to 1, with every division lit.
 * The enterprise layers read it from `useFrame` and turn it into per-division
 * progress; nothing renders on it, so the sequence costs no React work.
 */
export interface OpeningFrame {
  reveal: number
}

/**
 * The grade the shared stage renders at.
 *
 * The three tiers trade image for frame time: pixel ratio, the antialiasing
 * pass and the bloom are what a weak GPU cannot afford.
 */
export type QualityTier = 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'

input.content:
/**
 * The cold open's clock.
 *
 * One module owns every mark, because the claim card, the header counters and
 * the enterprise reveal are three readings of the same eighteen seconds and
 * must not drift apart. The marks are absolute milliseconds from the key press,
 * so a beat lands where it was written whatever the frame rate.
 */

/** How long the claim holds over a black stage before the first division lights. */
const CLAIM_MS = 4_400

/** How long the ten divisions take to light, from the first node to the last edge threading in. */
const IGNITE_MS = 10_200

/** When the graph starts to assemble. */
const IGNITE_AT = CLAIM_MS

/** When every division is lit. */
const REVEAL_AT = IGNITE_AT + IGNITE_MS

/** How long the claim takes to dissolve off the lit graph. */
export const DISSOLVE_MS = 1_400

/** The claim starts to go before the last division has finished, so the two beats overlap. */
const DISSOLVE_AT = REVEAL_AT - 1_000

/**
 * The whole sequence, from the key press to the claim gone.
 *
 * The camera's own settling flight runs after this, so the deck is at work
 * about eighteen seconds after the key.
 */
export const OPENING_MS = DISSOLVE_AT + DISSOLVE_MS

/**
 * The sequence under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: the claim card alone,
 * over a graph that is already whole.
 */
export const REDUCED_OPENING_MS = 4_000

/** How long the header counters take to climb from zero; they land as the last division lights. */
export const COUNTER_CLIMB_MS = REVEAL_AT

/**
 * What the claim card is doing.
 *
 * `black` is the stage behind the mark and the claim, `ignite` the same claim
 * over the assembling graph, and `out` the dissolve that leaves the deck.
 */
export type OpeningBeat = 'black' | 'ignite' | 'out'

/**
 * The beat at one point in the sequence.
 * @param elapsed - Milliseconds since the sequence started.
 * @param reduced - Whether the viewer asked for reduced motion, which has no ignition to sit over.
 * @returns The beat the card is on.
 */
export function openingBeat(elapsed: number, reduced: boolean): OpeningBeat {
  if (reduced) return elapsed < REDUCED_OPENING_MS ? 'black' : 'out'
  if (elapsed < IGNITE_AT) return 'black'
  if (elapsed < DISSOLVE_AT) return 'ignite'
  return 'out'
}

/**
 * How far the graph has assembled.
 * @param elapsed - Milliseconds since the sequence started.
 * @returns `0` with the graph dark, `1` with every division lit.
 */
export function openingReveal(elapsed: number): number {
  return Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (elapsed - IGNITE_AT) / IGNITE_MS))
}

4	 * Two kinds of state live here. React state (roster, runs, events, selection)
5	 * drives rendering. Frame state — `activity`, `bursts` and `openingFrame` — is
6	 * mutated in place and read from `useFrame`, because a sixty-times-a-second
7	 * render pass must not go through React at all.

36	type PresentationMode = 'off' | 'focus' | 'tour'

input.content:
feat(deck): a cold open that states the enterprise before it shows it

`O` takes the deck to the enterprise view and runs an eighteen-second cold
open, and `P` runs it as the tour's first act, once per page load. The stage
goes to black behind the Daliesk mark and one claim line composed only from
what the deck has read — agents, divisions, runs listed, certified today —
set with the title cards' kinetic type; the black then thins to the cards' own
gradient while the graph assembles behind it and the header counters climb
from zero, landing as the last division lights; the claim dissolves and the
working deck comes back with it.

The timing lives in `components/shell/opening.ts`, which the counters read
too, and the sequence writes its progress onto the store's frame state rather
than rendering: the stage reads it from `useFrame`. Any key and any click end
it at once — the store takes the reveal to whole, so the graph is never left
half lit — and the tour's step timer waits for the sequence, so the deck is
never navigated off an enterprise that is still arriving.

Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the claim holds for four seconds over a
graph already at rest, with no ignition to sit over.

input.content:
feat(deck): ignite the enterprise division by division

The enterprise stage reads the cold open's progress from the store's frame
state and turns it into one clock per division, in roster order: a division's
nodes scale up with a brief flare, its nebula comes up and overshoots with
them, and its relationships then thread out from their sources, waiting for
the later of the two divisions they join. The leader lines follow at the end
of the reveal and the division names wait for the sequence, so a graph still
arriving is never labelled as though it were done.

Nothing new runs per frame. The node layers fold the reveal into writes the
frame loop already made, and the edge layer carries it in its material: each
vertex knows when its edge lights and where it sits along its arc, so a whole
division threads in on one uniform write. At rest every division reads as lit
and every flare as nothing, which is the same arithmetic on the same one code
path.

The camera holds the establishing shot through the ignition and flies down to
rest as the claim dissolves — the flight the deck already opened on. Traffic
and certificate bursts stay off until the graph is whole, because both read as
faults on an agent that is not lit yet.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

3	// Each visit settles, then times 90 consecutive animation frames and reports their median.
4	import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'

14	const PORT = Number(process.env.CDP_PORT ?? 9873)

17	// driving it would both corrupt this run and theirs.
18	try {
19	  const probe = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/version`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1500) })
20	  if (probe.ok) throw new Error(`port ${PORT} is already a devtools endpoint`)
21	} catch (error) {
22	  if (String(error).includes('already a devtools endpoint')) throw error
23	}

26	  '--headless=new',
27	  '--no-sandbox',
28	  '--disable-dev-shm-usage',
29	  '--enable-unsafe-swiftshader',
30	  '--hide-scrollbars',
31	  `--force-device-scale-factor=${DSF}`,
32	  `--window-size=${WIDTH},${HEIGHT}`,

34	  'about:blank',

36	chrome.stderr.on('data', () => {})

input.content:
fix(deck): keep the deck on screen when a view changes

react-three-fiber writes unknown props straight onto the object it mounts, so
`dispose={null}` on the tone-mapping primitive replaced the effect's own
`dispose` with `null`. The stage's cleanup then threw `dispose is not a
function` on unmount, React reported it to the nearest error boundary, and the
whole shell — header, stage, panel — went blank on the first view change.
Dropping the prop leaves the method alone; the reconciler never disposes a
primitive anyway, so the hook's own cleanup is still what frees the effect.

Every route change was affected, including the `1` / `2` / `3` keys, the nav
links, the presentation tour and the cold open's route home.

content.text:
Both features are in, gates are green, and the measurements are done. Here is the report.

## Commits (branch `worktree-agent-ab6cb053c8b65594b`, on top of `023d7c611`)

1. `235dc749e` — feat(deck): step the grade between three quality tiers
2. `cf55b563f` — feat(deck): a cold open that states the enterprise before it shows it
3. `be1ceda13` — feat(deck): ignite the enterprise division by division
4. `9290dee06` — docs(deck): say what the cold open and the quality ladder actually hold
5. `2f6e3cb35` — fix(deck): keep the deck on screen when a view changes

Note: my worktree was created from `master` (no `apps/command-deck`), so I reset the branch onto `023d7c611` before starting.

## Per file

- `deck/store.ts` — `OpeningPhase`/`OpeningFrame`/`QualityTier`; state `opening`, `openingAt`, `openingFrame` (mutable frame state, never rendered), `qualityTier`, `qualityPinned`; actions `startOpening(ignite)`, `endOpening()`, `setQualityTier`, `pinQualityTier`.
- `components/shell/opening.ts` (new) — the one home for the timeline: beat marks, `openingBeat`, `openingReveal`, `OPENING_MS`, `REDUCED_OPENING_MS`, `COUNTER_CLIMB_MS`.
- `components/shell/useOpening.ts` (new) — the rAF driver: writes `openingFrame.reveal`, returns the card's beat (3 React renders per sequence), and gives the card its dissolve even when the sequence is cut short.
- `components/shell/Opening.tsx` (new) — the claim card; composes the claim only from loaded data, carries its own black.
- `components/shell/kinetic.tsx` (new) — the per-letter type treatment (see "Shared changes").
- `components/shell/usePresentation.ts` — `O` key, `P` runs the opening as the tour's first act, any key/click ends it, tour timer gated on the sequence.
- `components/shell/RollingNumber.tsx` — counters climb from zero over the ignition; also now re-renders only when the drawn integer changes.
- `components/shell/DeckShell.tsx` — `data-opening` on the root, `<Opening />`, footer quality readout, `o open` hint.
- `app/globals.css` — `.opening` (veil → gradient → dissolve), the mark and claim type, and the rules that hold the tour's title card, the panel and the stage copy back during the sequence.
- `components/enterprise/reveal.ts` (new) — the ignition clock (per-division starts, `readIgnition`, `edgeLightsAt`) and `createEdgeMaterial`, the patched line material that threads edges in the vertex shader.
- `components/enterprise/arcs.ts` — `EdgeArc.lightsAt`; geometry gains `aLightsAt` and `aT`.
- `components/enterprise/AgentGraph.tsx`, `Constellations.tsx`, `GraphEdges.tsx`, `CertificateBursts.tsx`, `CameraRig.tsx` — read the reveal in `useFrame`; nodes/nebulae light per division with a flare, leader lines and names arrive at the end, traffic and bursts stay off until the graph is whole, the camera holds the establishing shot and flies down as the claim dissolves.
- `components/three/quality.ts` (new) — tier table, reduced grade, `qualityBounds`, `useQualityLadder`, `pinnedQuality`.
- `components/three/Stage.tsx` — dpr/SMAA/bloom from the tier, `PerformanceMonitor` when unpinned, and the `dispose={null}` removal.

## The cold open

Beats, in milliseconds from the key (constants in `components/shell/opening.ts`):

| t | beat |
|---|---|
| 0 | phase `playing`; the card goes up opaque over the stage; the mark and the claim arrive with the kinetic stagger; the panel and stage copy fade out; the counters take zero and start a 14.6 s climb |
| 0 – 4 400 | `black` |
| 4 400 | the black fades from under the card (1.1 s) and the graph starts to assemble; divisions light in roster order, each over 28% of the reveal, nodes first (flare peaking at 26% of its window) then edges threading from 45% |
| 13 600 | `out` — the claim dissolves over 1 400 ms |
| 14 600 | the last division completes; counters land |
| 15 000 | phase `done`; the camera flies establishing → rest over 2 500 ms; panel, stage copy, leader lines and division names come back |
| ≈17 500 | the working deck |

`O` starts it and routes to `/` first if you are elsewhere. `P` starts it as the tour's first act; the 30 s step timer does not start until the phase leaves `playing`, so the tour never navigates off a half-built graph. It runs once per page load — a second `P` starts the tour alone.

Ending early: every `keydown` calls `endOpening()` before doing its own work, and `pointerdown` does the same. `endOpening()` sets `openingFrame.reveal = 1` in the store, so the very next frame draws the whole graph — the reveal snaps to complete rather than freezing where it was. The card still leaves on its own 1.4 s dissolve, the counters finish at the ordinary 720 ms, and the camera flies down as if the sequence had run out. Verified on the production build: pressing `2` at ~5 s gives phase `done`, beat `out`, tour `off`, counters at 147/0/14 by 6.8 s, and the `2` key's own navigation still lands.

Reduced motion: `startOpening(false)` leaves the reveal at 1, the card holds ~4 s (cut in and out, since the reduced-motion media query already kills transitions), no per-division ignition, camera at rest.

| tier | dpr ceiling | SMAA | bloom intensity / radius |

| high | 1.75 | on | 1.35 / 0.78 |

`PerformanceMonitor` with `bounds = refreshrate > 90 ? [70, 100] : [45, 56]`. Hysteresis: 2 consecutive declines drop a tier, 4 consecutive inclines climb one, a run of one kind cancels the other, a tier holds 5 s after any change, and after 2 drops the tier reached becomes the ceiling and the grade stops climbing for the session. `?quality=high|medium|low` pins a tier and does not render the monitor at all. The footer reads `quality auto · high` / `quality pinned · low`. Under reduced motion the reduced grade (bloom 0.7, SMAA on, radius 0.78) overrides the tier, but the dpr still steps.

Observed on the production build, unpinned, under SwiftShader: `high` at 0–10 s → `medium` at 20 s → `low` at 40 s, then `low` held for the remaining 80 s with no oscillation.

## The extra fix

Leaving any view blanked the whole deck — header, stage and panel — on the baseline build too. `react-three-fiber` writes unknown props straight onto the object it mounts, so `dispose={null}` on the tone-mapping `<primitive>` replaced the effect's own `dispose` with `null`; the stage's unmount cleanup then threw `dispose is not a function`, React handed it to Next's error boundary, and the tree went. It hit the `1`/`2`/`3` keys, the nav links, the tour and the cold open's route home. Dropping the prop fixes it (a primitive is never disposed by the reconciler, so the hook still owns disposal). Verified before/after: baseline `/` → `/process` leaves `.deck` absent; HEAD keeps deck and canvas on `/` → `/process` and `/safety` → `/`.
